# TT and SS are $\star3$ on the Möbius strip with $n+1$ pawns for every $n\ge11$: the insertion proof of Note 5 of Section S15, with the arc at the seam

**Summary**

1. **Theorem.** In the whole-board pawn game on the Möbius strip $M_n$ with the rules of Note 5 (section 1 there: e.p. on, an e.p.-capturable pawn is not passed, the game ends at the first passed pawn, race rule "count" with ties against the mover):
   - $TT(m)=B5\,W2\,W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2\,(B4\,W2)^m$ ($n=2m+10$, $n+1$ pawns) is $\star3$ for every $m\ge1$;
   - $SS(m)=B6\,W3\,(W2\,B4)^m\,W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2\,B4$ ($n=2m+11$, $n+1$ pawns) is $\star3$ for every $m\ge0$.

   Here "$G$ is $\star3$" means: $G+\star h$ and $\star3+\star h$ have the same outcome for every nim-heap $\star h$ (P for $h=3$, N otherwise). Together the families give a $\star3$ ring with $n+1$ pawns on $M_n$ for every even $n\ge12$ (TT) and every odd $n\ge11$ (SS).
2. **Method.** The insertion proof of Note 5, with its statement V and Lemmas 1, 2, 3 cited, not re-proved. Both walls are type E walls of Note 5 (single pawns alternating $W2$/$B4$); no colour reversal $\kappa$ is used. Cuts and bases: TT $c=14$, arc $10..19$, $m_0=5$ ($n=20$); SS $c=6$, arc $2..11$, $m_0=6$ ($n=23$). Smaller $m$ by direct search.
3. **The seam.** At the TT base the arc ends at the seam file $19=n-1$, and the file across the seam, file 0, is in the zone (it changes in 435 of 1305 nodes). This is the mirror image of the endpoint case $c-4=0$ of Note 5, which its Lemma 3 already covers ($4\le c\le n-6$ with equality). The exterior neighbour may change between reduced nodes. At each node insertion preserves the actual contents on both sides of the seam and the reflected view across it (section 2).
4. Status: **PROVED** for $m\ge m_0$ given C1, and for smaller $m$ by C2 (CHECKED-2). C1 is CHECKED-2.

## 0. Result and labels

PROVED = hand proof complete, given the cited lemmas and the named finite facts. COMPUTED-1 = one program. CHECKED-$k$ = $k$ independently written programs agree. Programs: **R** = the reduced-graph program R of Note 5, run on a faster drop-in for its move generator and adjudicator; **M1**, **M2** = two of the three solvers of the scans of Section S6.4, as in Note 5 (called for values only, one ring per process). Let $\mathrm{start}_m$ be the displayed family word with its starting directions and no e.p. right, and let $R_m$ be its reduced game (Note 5, section 1). For a given mover, T wins immediately, L loses immediately, P permits an immediate winning terminal reply, and K is any remaining move. The graph follows K-moves of either colour and stores K-children and the existence of a T-move separately for each colour. An unqualified pawn flag is an e.p. right. A signature lists outcomes in increasing heap size. N means the starter wins, P means the starter loses, and L means White wins with either starter.

**C1.** CHECKED-2. An independent program written by a model of another vendor, on its own rules implementation (the referee's program of Note 5, extended; it uses no code of R, of the drop-in, of M1 or of M2) reproduced both sets of C1 statistics and signatures: $TT(5)$: 1305 nodes, 4018 K-edges, 1212 T-moves, no flagged node, no node with a passer, zone $\{0,1,3..8\}$, NNNPN; $SS(6)$: 22755, 72730, 49694, none, none, zone $\{0,1,12,13,15..22\}$, NNNPN. Each program also checked its own rooted insertion isomorphism at the base cut ($\mathrm{ins}_{14}$ from $TT(5)$ onto $TT(6)$ and $\mathrm{ins}_6$ from $SS(6)$ onto $SS(7)$: roots, nodes, K-children and T-flags per side); the independent program tests exact insertion within its own implementation and does not compare node identities with R. It also confirmed the seam facts of section 2 (no capture across the seam in any node of $TT(5)$; in $SS(6)$ 1705 and 1640 captures across it, all of class T), and C2 by its own whole-board search (a third program for every line of C2).

## 1. Families, walls, cuts

Files $0..n-1$ form the chart; the seam joins file $n-1$ to file $0$. Pattern file, wall, $\mathrm{ins}_c$ (new files $c+1,c+2$ hold copies of files $c+1,c$; old files $\ge c+1$ shift by 2) and "far" are as in Note 5, sections 1 and 3.

| | $TT(m)$, $n=2m+10$ | $SS(m)$, $n=2m+11$ |
|---|---|---|
| fixed part | files $0..9$: $B5\,W2\,W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2$ | files $0,1$: $B6\,W3$; files $2m+2..2m+10$: $W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2\,B4$ |
| wall (type E) | files $10..n-1$: $B4$ even, $W2$ odd | files $2..2m+1$: $W2$ even, $B4$ odd |
| seam neighbours (file $n-1$ / file 0) | $W2$ (wall) / $B5$ (zone) | $B4$ (zone) / $B6$ (zone) |
| proposed zone $Z_m$ (the union of files differing from the root across K-reachable nodes; finite rows in section 4, propagation in section 3) | $\{0,1,3..8\}$ for $m\ge1$ | $\{0,1\}\cup\{2m,2m+1\}\cup\{2m+3..n-1\}$ for $m\ge4$ |
| cut, arc $c-4..c+5$ | $c=14$, $10..19$ | $c=6$, $2..11$ |
| arc inside wall $\setminus Z_m$ iff | $n-1\ge19$: $m\ge5$ | $2m-1\ge11$: $m\ge6$ |
| $\mathrm{ins}_c(\mathrm{start}_m)$ | inserts copies of files 15 ($W2$), 14 ($B4$) after file 14: $\mathrm{start}_{m+1}$ for $m\ge3$ | inserts copies of files 7 ($B4$), 6 ($W2$) after file 6: $\mathrm{start}_{m+1}$ for $m\ge3$ |
| $\mathrm{ins}_c(Z_m)$ (old indices) | $Z_m$ (all $<15$) $=Z_{m+1}$ | $\{0,1\}$ fixed, $\{2m,2m+1\}\to\{2m+2,2m+3\}$, $\{2m+3..2m+10\}\to\{2m+5..2m+12\}$: $Z_{m+1}$ ($m\ge4$) |

**Phase.** Note 5 defines a type E wall as single pawns alternating $W2$ (up) and $B4$ (down) on a chart interval; the parity of the phase is not part of the definition, and Lemma 2's proof treats $q=W2$ and $q=B4$ separately, each with the other pattern pawn on both neighbours. TT has the phase of Note 5's F1, F2 ($B4$ even); SS has the opposite phase ($W2$ even). Both are type E, so Lemmas 2 and 3 apply as stated; $\kappa$ (needed in Note 5 only for type O, F3) is not used. The mirror $f\mapsto n-1-f$ enters only inside Note 5's proof of Lemma 2 (the window $j-3..j+1$). Insertion keeps the phase: TT's new files 15, 16 hold $W2$, $B4$ between $B4$ (14) and $W2$ (old 15, now 17); SS's new files 7, 8 hold $B4$, $W2$ between $W2$ (6) and $B4$ (old 7, now 9).

**Lemma 3's range** ($4\le c\le n-6$): TT $c=14$, $n\ge20$ (equality $c=n-6$ at $n=20$); SS $c=6$, $n\ge23$.

## 2. The seam

The seam enters a pawn's moves, flag and passed status only through the view of a pawn on file $0$ or $n-1$ (Note 5, section 1, View). We go through the places where Note 5 uses the arc or its surroundings.

- **V** needs only that $0\le c<c+1\le n-1$ and files $c,c+1$ are consecutive pattern files of one wall in its single phase. (V1)'s proof replaces the chart pair $(c,c+1)$ and keeps the seam pair $(n-1,0)$, now $(n+1,0)$, with the same contents and the same mirroring, whatever those contents are. For TT, $c+1=15<19$; for SS, $c+1=7$.
- **Lemma 2** is used for central pawns on files $c-3..c+4$ (TT: $11..18$; SS: $3..10$), with windows $j-1..j+3$ or $j-3..j+1$ inside the arc. Its proof reads the contents of the window's files, the views of the window's interior files, and the view of the capturer on file $j$. For TT's $j=18$ (window $15..19$) the capturer's view is files $17,18,19$, all chart files; the departure square on file 17 is seen from files $16..18$ only. File 19's own view, which contains file 0 across the seam, is never read. So nothing in Lemma 2 depends on file 0.
- **Lemma 3.** Far files are $f\le c-4$ or $f\ge c+5$ in chart coordinates: TT $\{0..10\}\cup\{19\}$ at $n=20$, SS $\{0,1,2\}\cup\{11..n-1\}$. In (ii) a far first move changes its own file and its capture target, a chart neighbour or the seam neighbour; from file 19 these are 18 ($=c+4$) or 0, from file 0 they are 1 or 19. In (iii) a far reply changes files $\le c-1$ or $\ge c+2$, a seam capture changes files 0 and $n-1$, and an e.p. capturer is a chart or seam neighbour of a far stepper. After the far first move, files $c-2..c+3$ still have their pattern contents. If the child is live, replies from $c-1..c+2$ are near and cannot win immediately by Lemma 2(a). All other replies are far and have matching moves on the enlarged board. Such a reply can change a file of $c-2..c+3$, but it leaves $c,c+1$ intact, so insertion commutes with it and V3 compares its winner. The arc endpoints satisfy the parent pattern hypothesis. The exterior seam neighbour may vary from node to node. Note 5's bracketed seam remarks ("both are far, since $0\le c-4$ and $n-1\ge c+5$") cover the case $c+5=n-1$ exactly as they cover $c-4=0$.
- **Answer.** No step uses that the seam neighbour of the arc's end file is a pattern file or is unchanged. In Note 5's F1, F2 that neighbour (file $n-1$) happens to be frozen; for TT at $n=20$ it is file 0, a zone file, and the lemmas still apply. For $m>5$, TT's arc $10..19$ is interior ($n-1\ge21$) and the question does not arise. SS's arc $2..11$ is interior for every $m\ge6$; files 0, 1 (zone) and the seam lie on the far side of file 2, and the seam captures between files 0 and $n-1$ (both far) are matched by (ii), (iii).

**Computed corroboration (S).** $TT(5)$: in all 1305 nodes the arc $10..19$ equals the start and there is no flag; file 0 differs from the start in 435 nodes, file 19 in none; the pawn on file 19 has exactly two moves per node, $W2\to3$ and $W2\to4$, both P (2610 moves); no capture across the seam exists in any node; no K-move touches the arc. Moreover the strip and cylinder reduced graphs of $TT(5)$ coincide: the same 1305 positions, the same K-children and T-counts. These are the numbers of C1T in Note 4 for $T_{20}$, which is $TT(5)$ rotated. $SS(6)$: in all 22755 nodes the arc $2..11$ equals the start, no flag; captures across the seam occur (1705 from file 0, 1640 from file 22), all T, both files far; no K-move touches the arc. Unlike TT, SS's strip graph differs from the cylinder's (22755 versus 40445 nodes for $S_{23}$ in Note 4): the seam acts inside the zone.

## 3. Invariant and step

**H (start).** $\mathrm{start}_m$ has no flag (no pawn has just double-stepped) and no passed pawn (C1 for the base; for $m>m_0$ by V3 and $\mathrm{ins}_c(\mathrm{start}_m)=\mathrm{start}_{m+1}$).

**Invariant $I_m$** (Note 5, section 4): no node of $R_m$ has a flag, and every node agrees with $\mathrm{start}_m$ outside $Z_m$.

**Step.** Let $m\ge m_0$ and $I_m$. Every node $p$ of $R_m$ is non-terminal (root or K-child) and has no flag. The arc lies in the wall and avoids $Z_m$ (section 1 table), so its files carry exactly their start content: pattern files of one wall, in its single phase. The arc is a chart interval ($c-4\ge0$, $c+5\le n-1$). So Lemma 3 applies to every node with the family's fixed $c$, and $\mathrm{ins}_c(\mathrm{start}_m)=\mathrm{start}_{m+1}$. Insertion is injective by deleting the two copies. Since every old K-edge lifts and every K-edge out of an image lifts back, induction on path length from the corresponding roots (Note 5, section 4) gives: the nodes of $R_{m+1}$ are the images of those of $R_m$, with K-children and T-flags mapped. Images have no flag and agree with $\mathrm{start}_{m+1}$ outside $\mathrm{ins}_c(Z_m)=Z_{m+1}$, since the inserted files are copies of pattern files. So $I_{m+1}$ and $R_{m+1}\cong R_m$. For SS the zone moves with $m$; the check that the moved zone is the next zone, including the wall-end files $2m,2m+1$, is the last table row of section 1 (valid for $m\ge4$, in particular $m\ge6$).

**C3** (extra). R found $\mathrm{ins}_c(R_m)=R_{m+1}$ for every cut $c$ with $c,c+1$ in TT's wall at the steps $m\to m+1$, $m=1..7$. For SS at the steps $m\to m+1$, $m=4,5,6$, it holds for $c=2..2m-2$ and fails at $c=2m-1,2m$, the two cuts whose copied files reach the zone (not admissible); at $m=1,2,3$ the SS graphs are not yet stable (node counts 18649, 28307, 24837, then 22755 from $m=4$). Admissible cuts reported by the same runs: TT at $m=5$: $\{14\}$; SS at $m=6$: $\{6\}$. M1 and M2 also give NNNP for TT $m=5..11$ and SS $m=6..10$ (beyond what the proof needs).

## 5. Theorem and proof

**Theorem.** $TT(m)\equiv\star3$ for every $m\ge1$ and $SS(m)\equiv\star3$ for every $m\ge0$: $G+\star h$ has the outcome of $\star3+\star h$ for every nim-heap $\star h$. Hence $M_n$ carries a $\star3$ ring with $n+1$ pawns for every $n\ge11$.

*Proof.* Let $G$ be TT or SS, $m\ge m_0$. $I_{m_0}$ is C1 (with section 1 for the zone and arc). Section 3 gives $I_m$ and $R_m\cong R_{m_0}$, with T-flags, for every $m\ge m_0$. The outcome of $R+\star h$ depends only on the graph, its T-flags and $h$, so by C1 it is N, N, N, P for $h=0,1,2,3$ with either player to move first; by Lemma 1 of Note 5 (the start is non-terminal) so is that of $G(m)+\star h$. For $h\ge4$ the player to move takes the heap to $\star3$; the pawn position, which has no flag, is kept, and $G(m)+\star3$ is P, so $G(m)+\star h$ is N. These are the outcomes of $\star3+\star h$: P exactly for $h=3$. For $m<m_0$ (TT $m=1..4$, SS $m=0..5$) C2 gives NNNP for $h\le3$, and $h\ge4$ follows as before. TT covers $n=2m+10$, every even $n\ge12$; SS covers $n=2m+11$, every odd $n\ge11$. $\blacksquare$

## 6. Scope and self-check

**Not claimed.** Other race rules; the component-sum model; equality with $\star3$ as a standard partizan game or against addends other than nim-heaps (as in Note 4, H7). $n=10$ with 11 pawns is open: $TT(0)$ is LLLL, the targeted search found $\star3$ rings with 12 pawns but none with 11. $n=9$ is covered by the previously known ring, not by these families. The further $n+1$ families H2 (odd $n=9..31$) and E2 (even $n=12..32$) are CHECKED-2 only (M1, M2): their sampled reduced graphs include e.p.-flagged nodes, so the no-flag hypotheses of Lemma 2(b) and Lemma 3 fail there. Lemma 2(a) has its own flag condition. No all-width induction for these families is supplied.

**Weakest points.**
1. **C1.** C1 is CHECKED-2 at both bases. R and the independent program use separate rules implementations and agree on the counts, zones, absence of flags and passers, and heap signatures. Each also checked its own rooted insertion isomorphism at the base cut. The computations share the same written rules.
2. **The arc at the seam (TT, $n=20$).** Section 2 argues that Lemma 3's case $c+5=n-1$ is covered by Note 5's proof as written, and that file 0 changing is irrelevant. Note 5's family bases F1 and F2 use the left endpoint with a frozen seam neighbour. Its random test pooled the two endpoints. Here file 0 actually changes, while the TT(5) strip census found no crossing captures and only P pushes from file 19. If in doubt, one can avoid it: take $m_0=6$ for TT ($n=22$, arc $10..19$ interior), with $TT(5)$ moved into C2 (M1, M2 give NNNP); the C1 line for $m=6$ has the same numbers and zone. This alternative base is also CHECKED-2: the independent program reproduces the $m=6$ base graph (1305 / 4018 / 1212, no flag, no passer, the same zone, NNNPN) and the direct signature NNNP of $TT(5)$.
3. **SS's base is the larger graph** (22755 nodes) and its zone contains two wall files that move. At SS(6) the arc ends at 11, immediately before zone file 12. Among tested cuts with both copied files in the wall, precisely those whose copied pair meets the zone failed at steps $m=4,5,6$. Other cuts whose ten-file arc meets the zone can pass the finite test. The proof uses only cut 6 from $m=6$ onward.
